READ LATER SEE ALL Remove French President Emmanuel Macron (centre right), French European Space Agency astronaut Thomas Pesquet (centre) and Greece’s Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis (centre left) pose with aerospace professionals during the International Space Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris, on September 9, 2026. | Photo Credit: AP The two-day International Space Summit got underway in Paris on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) in the presence of French President Emmanuel Macron. Mr. Macron said that the summit will see the participation of 90 countries, and more than 50 projects are expected to be signed, bringing in billions of investments. “This space summit is a unique opportunity for all. More than 50 projects are expected to be signed during the summit. Projects between France and Germany and France and the UAE will be signed. There will be a lot of big investments. We also confirm the Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite (IRIS²), which is a very important big programme for us in Europe. We will have a series of meetings, common investments, common programmes and partnerships to strengthen European space,” Mr. Macron said. Greek astronaut Adrianos Golemis, a flight surgeon, was announced as the first astronaut from Greece to embark on a private mission to the International Space Station (ISS). France’s President Emmanuel Macron, French European Space Agency (ESA) astronaut Thomas Pesquet and Greece’s Prime Minister Kyriakos pose with astronauts and members of the Vast space programme during the International Space Summit at the Grand Palais in Paris. | Photo Credit: Reuters “It is a very special moment for Greece, and I do believe that Adrianos, apart from the very interesting experiments which he will conduct onboard the ISS, will be a true inspiration for young Greek kids to focus on science and technology, engineering, and mathematics and to dream again and move away from screens and not be attached to social media,” the Prime Minister of Greece, Kyriakos Mitsotaki, said. The flight will be part of the first private astronaut mission to the ISS that NASA awarded to Vast, a private American aerospace company. French astronaut Thomas Pesquet will be the commander of the Vast mission, and astronaut Aleš Svoboda will be the pilot. The mission is planned for 2027 on the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft and will be launched onboard the Falcon 9 rocket. India’s participation ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan led an Indian delegation to the summit and is expected to meet various space agencies and companies. “We have come for the summit here in Paris. We met officials from Hungary today and are expected to meet ESA officials and other delegations which are participating in the meeting,” Dr. Narayanan told The Hindu . (This reporter is in Paris at the invitation of France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs to cover the International Space Summit). https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/23/us-d.text: The United States designated helium as a critical material on Friday, citing its essential role in semiconductor manufacturing and energy production, as well as growing concerns over disruptions to global supplies.The move by the US Department of Energy will make additional federal funding available to helium producers and bring the material under closer government monitoring.Helium is mainly extracted as a byproduct of natural gas processing. The US is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, with Qatar and Russia also among the leading helium producers.Helium exports from Qatar have been severely disrupted by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid its war with Israel and the US. Iranian strikes on Qatari infrastructure have further affected supplies, while Russia introduced temporary export restrictions in April to protect its domestic market.US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Trump administration was seeking to reduce dependence on foreign sources of critical materials, boost domestic manufacturing, support American jobs and strengthen economic and national security.“President Trump is bringing back America’s manufacturing industry, and that means making sure we have the materials needed to build things in America again,” Wright said in a statement.Europe faces mounting pressure on helium suppliesWhile the US is seeking to strengthen domestic production, Europe has faced growing difficulties securing helium supplies, compounded by China's decision in July to impose a temporary export ban on the gas.Although China is not a major helium producer, it has served as a transit hub for Russian supplies reaching Europe, according to a July report by the Financial Times.The EU banned direct imports of Russian helium in 2024, but some supplies reportedly continued to reach European markets through China.
